title: LLM prefetch & routing ideas (scratchpad)
content:
Context / goal:
- Rough brainstorming doc for prefetching KV/cache + request routing ideas to reduce tail latency and token cost for chat-like workloads.
- Focus: low-risk experiments we can run on Dedicated/Hosted to validate latency wins and cost impact. Keep API surface minimal.

Problem statements / pain: 
- Chat workloads with medium context lengths (1k-3k tokens) have high repeat prefix work across users -> wasted compute.
- Cold-start / first-token latency spikes when KV cache isn't warmed (long-tail p99).
- Routing currently only by model + region + tier; not workload-aware. Some requests would benefit from routing to slightly cheaper/quantized variants if quality similar.
- Need safe fallbacks when prefetch/cache misses or when model variant mismatch occurs.

Constraints / principles:
- Non-breaking for existing API users. Opt-in experiments first.
- Safety: no user-data leaks across caches or tenants. Tenant isolation enforced.
- Observable: metric surface for cost delta, p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit rate, quality regressions (eval prompt set).
- Small incremental ops complexity at first (feature flags, canary rollout).

Proposed ideas (high level):
1) Lightweight prefix prefetching (client-hinted):
   - Client sends a small "prefetch_hint" blob with early turns (e.g., system + first user prompt). Server precomputes KV cache for common model and stores ephemeral cache keyed by session-id/hash.
   - TTL short (minutes) and per-tenant. Eviction policy LRU.
   - Use primarily for interactive flows (chat sessions).
   - Expected benefit: reduced first-token generation latency for sequential messages, fewer redundant KV computations.

2) Server-side proactive prefetch (heuristic):
   - On patterns that predict follow-up messages (e.g., user engaged, recent typing activity, streaming partials), server triggers prefetch for next-turn candidates.
   - Risk: wasted work for abandoned sessions. Mitigation: short TTL, only prefetch small KV summaries (not full large caches), budgeted per-tenant.

3) Workload-aware routing to model variants:
   - Add routing rule type: "quality-tolerance" (low/medium/high) per route. Low tolerance routes can be served by quantized/cheaper variants if eval score within threshold.
   - Routing decision uses SLA (latency budget), cost target, and historical eval similarity.
   - Fallback stack: primary (high-precision), secondary (quantized), fallback to primary if quality drop detected.

4) Hybrid batching + cache reuse:
   - Continuous batching remains, but prefer grouping requests that share prefix hashes to reuse cached KV across batch members.
   - Need fast prefix hash matching at ingress.

Rough user stories:
- As an app developer, I want optional prefetch hints so my chat UI can warm the model before sending the next message, so response feels instant to my users.
- As a platform engineer, I want to route low-risk routes to quantized variants automatically to save costs while maintaining quality within an agreed threshold.
- As an SRE, I want clear metrics and rollout toggles so I can disable prefetching if it increases cost/instability.

Acceptance criteria / metrics to monitor:
- Latency: reduce p95 initial token latency for chat sessions by >=20% in canary cohort.
- Cost: net token compute cost per session should not increase >5% (ideally decrease). Track per-tenant.
- Quality: automatic A/B on eval prompt set shows BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval metric within tolerance (<2% degradation) for routes using quantized variants.
- Cache hit rate targets: >=40% for hint-prefetched sessions within TTL.

Experiment plan (phased):
Phase 0: offline sims + instrumentation (2 weeks)
- Simulate prefetch benefit on historical traces (compute expected KV reuse).
- Add metrics hooks: prefetch requests, cache hits, TTL expirations, wasted prefetch seconds.

Phase 1: client-hinted prefetch alpha (4 weeks)
- Expose opt-in prefetch_hint field to SDK. Server stores ephemeral cache. Canary to 5% of orgs that opt-in.
- Collect metrics and manual QA.

Phase 2: server-side heuristic prefetch (4-6 weeks)
- Enable for small set of customers with explicit budget. More aggressive telemetry.

Phase 3: routing/variant experiment (6-8 weeks)
- Add routing metadata quality-tolerance and model-variant table. Canary to internal apps first. Use eval harness to detect drift.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost accounting: how to charge for server-initiated prefetch compute? Billable? free? (probably free but counts against Dedicated compute budget). Need finance input.
- Data residency & privacy: ephemeral caches must not cross tenant or region boundaries. Encryption at rest? Ensure KMS usage for persistent caches (if any).
- Cache key design: what granularity? full prompt hash vs segmented chunking? Long prompts + system messages may reduce reuse.
- Eviction and memory pressure on Dedicated pools. How to prevent OOM attacks? throttling and per-tenant budgets.
- Observability: need synthetic prompts and eval prompt sets maintained. Who owns these sets? (product/research?)

Implementation notes / quick ideas:
- Use existing cache infra (if present) behind a "prefetch service" that exposes CreateCache(session_hash), GetCache(session_hash). Keep TTL short.
- For ingress: compute prefix-hash using normalized prompt (strip timestamps, client-only session metadata). Provide hashing util in SDKs.
- Routing: extend existing policy DSL with a quality_tolerance field; implement evaluator that scores candidate variants on small eval set before routing decisions.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with Aisha (applied-ml) on offline trace analysis to estimate win.
- Raise a short RFC for billing implications with finance/legal. (Owner: Priya)
- Prototype SDK prefetch_hint (JS + Python) to test UX.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft quick Jupyter on sample 10k session traces to compute potential cache reuse. -> in progress.
- Ask infra about a short-lived in-memory cache option on Dedicated (fast path).
- Add gating flag in console per-org to enable prefetching.

References / links:
- initial routing proposals PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proposals/pull/12
- related scratchpad: users/llm-prefetch-prd-scratchpad-aisha-khan (copy notes)

Random brainstorming fragments (unordered):
- Could we expose a "prefetch_prediction_score" to clients so they can voluntarily pay to have a session warmed? (monetization thought).
- Consider precomputing only first N layers of KV (cheap warm) and progressively fill rest if user continues -> tradeoffs.
- When routing to quantized variant, consider sampling 1/100 requests to verify quality by also running primary offline for comparison.

End of scratchpad.
